newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks hit all time high, market on a roll.
newsitem.headline: French stocks hit all time high, market on a roll.

text.p: The Paris bourse's blue chip CAC share index rose to an all time high of 2,805.37 points on Friday morning, propelled by Wall Street's overnight 1.8 percent rise and hopes of a ratification of a European stability pact at next week's EU Amsterdam summit, traders said.
The CAC-40 index was up 41.50 points or 1.5 percent at 2,801.77 at 0832 GMT after edging back from its high.
Volume was a busy 1.6 billion francs.
"There's a lot of volume out there," a broker said. He added that the message from the markets was that "in France, politics don't matter".

"The fundamentals are still very strong, with low inflation, momentum in the overall economy and a good earnings outlook," he said. Firms were sitting on cash mountains and could finance their investment rather than tapping the capital markets.
The Socialist government's insistence on a "social charter" attached to the stability pact was not such a bad idea, as high unemployment was destabilising, he added.

Investors who did not buy when the CAC index fell to 2,500 were now looking to get into the Paris market, which has lagged other European bourses by three or four percent in recent weeks, the broker said.

The general message from companies' annual shareholder meetings have been reassuring, with good volumes and reasonable profitability. "Profitability could be better" but French firms were generally competitive as reflected in the consistently strong trade surpluses, he added.
"I'm quite confident we will see 3,000 (on the CAC index) by the end of the year," he said.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's speech on general policy to the National Assembly on June 19 could be a trigger for profit-taking if the market keeps rising, the broker said.
Pinault-Printemps, up 3.87 percent to 2,875 francs, Carrefour, up 2.51 percent to 4,282, were among retailers favoured.
Elf Aquitaine was among the actives, up 2.07 percent at 642.
Renault firms 3.3 percent to 144.10 francs. The market considers that the government has taken a relatively "hands-off" approach on the Vilvoorde plant closure, a trader said.
Moulinex drops 1.33 percent, after Electrolux announcement of a restructuring plan which will close 25 plants and cut 12,000 jobs over two years.
Pernod Ricard lags the market, up 0.19 percent at 310.5. The drinks company said Spain's Larios had accepted it buyout offer, which had been long rumoured in the market.
Saint-Gobain firmed 1.31 percent to 850 after British abrasives maker Unicorn International agreed a recommended offer from the French firm valued at about 85.5 million stg.
